A SUPERSESSION NOTICE AND A PRIOR OCCUPANT IN ONE STRIP. Card 5 carries the archive correcting itself in public: "This paper SUPERSEDES THE STRUCTURAL FRAMING OF PHASE X IN ALL PRIOR ARCHIVE DEPOSITS. Phase X is a PHILOLOGICAL RECONSTRUCTION, NOT A THEORETICAL PROPOSAL." A retraction of the archive’s own earlier framing, retrieved as a source about the thing it reframes.

Card 4 is an exact prior use: FELIX HÖFLMAYER on Middle Bronze Age Jordan, where "PHASE X" designates a stratigraphic layer in Area III of an MB I city. Archaeology numbers its phases; the tenth is Phase X. A genuine occupant of the string, in a discipline that shares the archive’s vocabulary of strata and sequence and nothing else.

The July run of this string opened on the reconstruction as 'primarily' what the pairing means, named the Phase X Program and Operative Semiotics, and held the Bronze Age stratum and a fibre amplifier in a closing parenthesis. This run still says the string 'primarily points to' Marx, but to 'philological, philosophical, and historical reconstructions of Karl Marx's early writings' in the plural, with no work or author named, 'though it can occasionally appear in esoteric or scientific contexts'. It then takes the string apart token by token. 'Phase' finds the Adventist 'second and last phase' of Christ's ministry and a moon-phase calendar; 'X' finds the X-Ray in a Swift telescope paper; '1844' finds the Great Disappointment, the arXiv identifier 0803.1844 and a solenoid valve numbered X1844. Each fragment gets its own numbered section. The reconstruction keeps section 1, now headed by Marx's 'Feuerbachian Phase', and is recast twice. First, the title of #843, 'Phase X as Philological Reconstruction', is turned into a practice: 'scholarly efforts ... sometimes designate these missing developmental pieces as Phase X of Philological Reconstruction'. Second, the Medium card of #367 becomes a genre: 'in modern sociopolitical essays, "Phase X" is sometimes used metaphorically'. One author's work is spread into an anonymous plural. To give the other senses the same string, the composition supplies usages that no card carries. 'Esoteric or independent theological blogs occasionally use Phase X' has no source; the Adventist cards say 'phase', never 'Phase X'. The Swift paper is described as 'tracking gamma-ray burst "phases"', but its card is a status-and-performance report whose only link to the query is the digits of its arXiv number. 'Unique supermoon phases' is added to a card that says 13 full moons.
